marks.description: Several such regions on one picture, at most four

present.description: Only with card_id, for a card the human handed back to you. true: your work on it is done without rewording it, put the card before the human again. Ran `npm test`: 48 of 48 pass.
The slow one was the index on `orders`.

create_decision.title: Run the migration on production now?
create_decision.teaser: Locks orders for about 40 seconds; now, or tonight when nobody orders?

options.label: Now
options.detail: Short outage for whoever is online

sections.text: You asked why the deploy waits until 2. In short: the migration locks `orders`, and at 2 nobody is writing to it.
**Order of events.** Backup at midnight, migration at 2, deploy right after. The picture shows the three steps.
**If it fails,** the deploy does not start and you find a question from me in the morning.

revise_card.title: Run the migration tonight at 2?
revise_card.note: Running it now is off the table: the backup takes until midnight

merge_cards.title: Which parts of the storage plan do you agree to?

sections.text: Two machines show the same board. About two days more, and conflicts need a rule.

events.when: A new version of the connector is on disk (or the hub recommends one).
events.content: a sentence naming the version and what to do: file the update card (jetzt / später)

meta.version: the new version (a hash of the connector code, or the hub's recommended version)
meta.restart_required: "1" when only a restart loads it (/mcp → trommi → Reconnect), "0" when reload_connector can

events.example: <channel source="board" kind="update" update_available="1" version="3f2a9c1d0b7e" restart_required="0">A new version of the Trommi connector is available …</channel>

events.when: The human sent something (a message, an answer) in a format of a newer Trommi version than this connector reads.
events.content: a sentence saying so and that the connector needs an update; nothing of the unreadable part

optional.card_id: the card it was about, when it was one of yours

events.example: <channel source="board" kind="unsupported" update_required="1">The human sent something on the board that this Trommi connector is too old to read …</channel>

events.when: The human sent a chat message.
events.content: the message; when the human sent only files, a sentence naming them

optional.card_id: set when the human asks back about an open card instead of answering it; answer with reply and the same card_id
optional.handback: "1" when the human handed that card back to you to be reworked: revise it with revise_card, which presents it again
optional.explain: "1" when the human pressed "What??" (Explain) on that card: rework it with revise_card, and with a clip skill also attach a short silent clip of it (reply with card_id and the mp4)
optional.note: "1" when the message is one of the human's notes (the yellow slip from the Desk, the share sheet or a drop) sent to you: an answer he must not miss goes on his Desk as an info card (create_info), a bare acknowledgement stays a reply
optional.cards: ids of cards the human copied into this message, comma-separated, often another session's: each stands in full in the content (question, options, answer, notes, picture paths), so you can act on a decision you never saw
optional.cards_json: the same cards as a JSON list of {id, number, title, agent, choice_label, kind, status, choices}
optional.marks: how many notes and drawings the human pinned to parts of that card; they are lines of the content under "Notes pinned to the card:", and the picture of the annotated card is in image_path
optional.files: absolute paths of the files and pictures the human attached, comma-separated; open them
optional.image_path: the first attached picture, when there is one

events.example: <channel source="board" kind="chat">Please check the logs first.</channel>

events.when: The human answered a decision card.
events.content: the human's note, or a sentence naming the card and the chosen key; when the human wrote notes on single options, a blank line and "Notes on options:" follow, with one line "- Label [key], chosen: note" or "- Label [key], not chosen: note" per note, in the order of the options

meta.choice: key of the chosen option; of several, the first

optional.closed: "1" when the answer settled the card: every chosen option was one you marked final, so the card closed itself; nothing is expected of you, no close_card
optional.choices: only for a card made with multiple: true: every chosen key, comma-separated, in the order of the options
optional.trust: "1" when the human left the decision to you: choice is then the option you recommended, or empty if you recommended none; decide, say what you chose with reply and the card_id, and close the card
optional.marks: how many notes and drawings the human pinned to parts of the card; they are lines of the content under "Notes pinned to the card:"
optional.option_notes: only when the human wrote notes on single options: the keys that have one, comma-separated; the notes themselves are in the content
optional.files: absolute paths of what the human attached to the note of the answer, comma-separated
optional.image_path: the first attached picture, when there is one

events.example: <channel source="board" kind="decision" card_id="a1b2c3d4" choice="tonight">After the backup, please.</channel>

events.when: The human took an answer back; the card is open again.
events.content: a sentence saying which answer was taken back

meta.previous_choice: key of the answer that no longer holds

optional.previous_choices: only for a card made with multiple: true: every key that was chosen, comma-separated
optional.trust: "1" when what is taken back is the human leaving the decision to you
optional.shredded: "1" when the human took a card back out of the shredder; previous_choice is then empty

events.when: The human threw a question (or an info) away unanswered.
events.content: a sentence saying so and what to do: do not ask again, carry on with your own judgement or drop the matter; then the human's note, if they wrote one

optional.marks: how many notes and drawings the human pinned to the card before throwing it away; they are lines of the content
optional.files: absolute paths of the pictures that came with it, comma-separated

events.example: <channel source="board" kind="shredded" card_id="a1b2c3d4">The human threw the question "Which font?" away unanswered. …</channel>

events.when: The human read an info card (create_info) and closed it. Nothing is expected of you.
events.example: <channel source="board" kind="info_read" card_id="a1b2c3d4">The human read "How the nightly migration works" and closed it.</channel>

events.when: The human selected (or cut out) part of the Scribble Board and sent it to this session. What was sent left the board.
events.content: the words of the selected notes and spoken notes in reading order, or a sentence pointing at the picture

meta.board: the Scribble Board it came from (desk/<id>)
meta.message_id: the message in the conversation that shows the selection
meta.elements: ids of the selected strokes, notes and pictures, comma-separated
meta.image_path: PNG of exactly the selection, drawn from its strokes on white

events.example: <channel source="board" kind="scribble" board="desk/9d7f8611247c59b9c82e0c78b7f084a4" message_id="77" elements="d1/12/0,d1/14/2" image_path="/…/files/selection-9f2c41d07a3e.png">Ship the pad prototype</channel>

events.when: The human answered an approval card. Claude Code decides whether this or the terminal came first.
Claude Code wants approval for a tool call. It becomes a card with Allow and Deny, always on top of the stack.
Once, when the MCP connection starts. The name appears as "Program" in the sessions overview.

params.clientInfo.name: the program on the other end of stdio
